questions.stem: After heavy sweating, increased ADH most directly causes the collecting ducts to:
options: Become more permeable to water
Stop receiving filtrate
Secrete glucose into urine
Destroy the medullary gradient
questions.explanation: ADH promotes insertion of aquaporins, increasing water reabsorption from the collecting ducts and producing a smaller volume of concentrated urine.

questions.stem: The countercurrent arrangement of the loop of Henle is most important for establishing:
options: A high glucose concentration in urine
An osmotic gradient in the renal medulla
A pressure gradient in the aorta
An acidic environment in the stomach
questions.explanation: Opposing flow and different permeabilities in the loop multiply a medullary osmotic gradient, which later allows water reabsorption from collecting ducts.

questions.stem: In a negative-feedback pathway, an effective response must ultimately:
options: Amplify the original deviation
Operate without a receptor
Move the regulated variable back toward its set range
Continue unchanged after balance returns
questions.explanation: Negative feedback opposes the initial change. The response diminishes as the regulated condition returns toward its normal range.

questions.stem: Selective destruction of pancreatic beta cells most directly impairs the response to:
options: Falling blood glucose through glucagon
Rising body temperature through sweating
Falling water potential through ADH
Rising blood glucose through insulin
questions.explanation: Beta cells secrete insulin when blood glucose rises. Loss of these cells weakens glucose uptake and storage, allowing hyperglycaemia.

questions.stem: A regulated variable moves away from its normal range. Which outcome follows most directly?
options: Corrective responses oppose the original disturbance
Sweat production increases and the skin cools
Heat loss from the body surface increases
Heat transfer from core blood to the environment decreases
questions.explanation: Corrective responses oppose the original disturbance. Negative feedback reduces the error detected by receptors and control centres.
